wedding. Now there is no egg, no
cake, and no gift. What will my
sister say?”
translation: “Ngefi wacita?” efyailishenye Vusi. “Icaani ico caciba buupe bwakwa nkashi yandi. Bakakuula bacimpela icaani pantu bacikontola icimuti icacifuma ku bacilatoola ifitwalo. Abacilatoola ifitwalo bacimpeela icimuti pantu bacitoba ilini ilyakupangila keeke yakwa nkashi yandi. Keeke yaciba no kuba yapa bwinga bwakwe. Nomba tapali ilini, tapali keeke, elyo kabili tapali no bupe. Nkashi yandi alaayalanda shani? ”

english:
The cow was sorry she was greedy.
The farmer agreed that the cow
could go with Vusi as a gift for his
sister. And so Vusi carried on.
translation: Iŋombe yalilomba ubwelelo pali ubu buliili. Umulimi alisumine ukuti Vusi asende iŋombe nga ubupe bwakwa nkashi yakwe. Efyo Vusi akonkenyepo.

english:
But the cow ran back to the farmer
at supper time.
And Vusi got lost on his journey.
He arrived very late for his sister’s
wedding. The guests were already
eating.
translation: Lelo iŋombe yalibutwike no kubwelela ku mulimi ilyo inshita ya kulya icakulya ca mulalilo yafikile. Vusi nao alilubile pa bulendo bwakwe. Aafikile ku bwinga bwakwa nkashi yakwe ubushiku saana. Abaitilwe ku bwinga ninshi nabatampa no kulya.

english:
“What shall I do?” cried Vusi.
“The cow that ran away was a gift,
in return for the thatch the builders
gave me. The builders gave me the
thatch because they broke the stick
from the fruit pickers. The fruit
pickers gave me the stick because
they broke the egg for the cake.
The cake was for the wedding. Now
there is no egg, no cake, and no
gift.”
translation: “Nalacita shani?” efyailishenye Vusi. “lIya ŋombe ibutwike yaciba buupe, pa caani bakakuula bampeele. Bakakuula bacimpeela icaani pantu bacikontola icimuti icacifuma ku bacilatoola ifitwalo. Abacilatoola ifitwalo bacimpeela icimuti pantu bacitoba ilini lyakupangila keeke. Keeke yaciba no kuba yapa bwinga. Nomba tapali ilini, tapali keeke, kabili tapali no bupe.”

english:
Vusi’s sister thought for a while,
then she said,
“Vusi my brother, I don’t really care
about gifts. I don’t even care about
the cake! We are all here together, I
am happy. Now put on your smart
clothes and let’s celebrate this
day!”
And so that’s what Vusi did.
translation: Nkashi yakwa Vusi alikutumene panshita iitali, elyo asosa ati, “Nshisakamene pa fyabupe, nangu pali keeke! Nintemwe pantu bonse tuli kuno kabili tuli abansansa. Nomba fwaleni ifyakufwala fyenu ifisuma tusefye ubu bushiku!” Nacine efyo Vusi aacitile.

english:
Grandma’s garden was wonderful, full of sorghum, millet, and cassava.

But best of all were the bananas.

Although Grandma had many grandchildren, I secretly knew that I was her favourite. She invited me often to her house. She also told me little secrets.

But there was one secret she did not share with me: where she ripened bananas.
translation: Ibala lyaba maama lyali ilisuma saana, mwali amasaka, amale, na tuute. Nomba ifyawamishe pali fyonse ni nkonde. Nangula bamaama bakwete abeshikulu abengi, nalishibe ukuti nine batemwishishe. Balenjita lyonse ku ŋanda ku mwabo. Baaleenshimikilako no twankama tumo-tumo. Nomba kwali inkama imo iyo bashanjebeleko: uko balefumbika inkonde.

english:
One day I saw a big straw basket placed in the sun outside Grandma’s house. When I asked what it was for, the only answer I got was, “It’s my magic basket.”

Next to the basket, there were several banana leaves that Grandma turned from time to time. I was curious. “What are the leaves for, Grandma?” I asked. The only answer I got was, “They are my magic leaves.”
translation: Bushiku bumo namwene bamaama nababika icimuseke pa kasuba panse ya ŋanda. Ilyo nabepwishe batiile “Muuseke wankama.” Mupepi no museke paali amabuula ya nkonde ayenji ayo bamaama baaleepilibula kashita-kashita. Naleefwaisha ukwishiba, efyo nabepwishe nati, “Mabuula yanshi aya maama?” Banjaswikefye abati “Mabuula ya nkama yandi.”

english:
It was so interesting watching Grandma, the bananas, the banana leaves and the big straw basket. But Grandma sent me off to my mother on an errand.

“Grandma, please, let me watch as you prepare…”

“Don’t be stubborn, child, do as you are told,” she insisted. I took off running.
translation: Caliweme ukutamba bamaama, inkonde, amabuula ya nkonde, no museke uukulu. Nomba bamaama epakuntuma ukuli bamaayo. Elyo nabeba nati, “Maama napaapaata lekeni imoneko ifyo mucita…” Bamaama epakuti, “We mwanawe uleumfwa, cita ifyo nakweba endesha.” Efyo naile ulubilo.

english:
When I returned, Grandma was sitting outside but with neither the basket nor the bananas.

“Grandma, where is the basket, where are all the bananas, and where…”

But the only answer I got was, “They are in my magic place.” It was so disappointing!
translation: Ilyo nabwelele, nasangile bamaama nabekala panse, nomba tapaali inkonde nangu umuseke. “Maama, umuseke ulikwisa, ne nkonde shilikwi, nga…” Bamaama epakuti, “Fili kuncende yandi iyankama.” Nshatemenwe.

english:
Two days later, Grandma sent me to fetch her walking stick from her bedroom.

As soon as I opened the door, I was welcomed by the strong smell of ripening bananas. In the inner room was grandma’s big magic straw basket. It was well hidden by an old blanket. I lifted it and sniffed that glorious smell.
translation: Panuma ya nshiku shibili, bamaama bantumine mukusenda inkonto yabo ku muputule. Cilya naisulafye iciibi, akaceena kankonde ishapya kampokelela. Kukati ekwali umuseke wa nkaama. Ninshi nabafisa bwino-bwino mu bulangeti bwakale. Nafimbulapo nanunshako akaceena akasuma.

english:
Grandma’s voice startled me when she called, “What are you doing? Hurry up and bring me the stick.”

I hurried out with her walking stick. “What are you smiling about?” Grandma asked.

Her question made me realise that I was still smiling at the discovery of her magic place.
translation: Ishiwi lyaba maama epakuntinya lintu banjutile. “Finshi ulecita? Endesha ndetela inkonto.” Efyo naendeshe ukutwala inkoto. Bamaama epakunjipusha ati, “Finshi uleseka.” Cilya banjipusha elyo naibukisha ukuti ncili ndesekelela pa kusanga incende yankama yaba maama.

english:
The following day when grandma came to visit my mother, I rushed to her house to check the bananas once more.

There was a bunch of very ripe ones. I picked one and hid it in my dress. After covering the basket again, I went behind the house and quickly ate it. It was the sweetest banana I had ever tasted.
translation: Ubushiku bwakonkelepo, elyo bamaama baishile mukupempula bamaayo, nabutukile ku mwabo mukumona inkonde na kabili. Nasangile umusemo wa nkonde ishapya. Nasendako lumo nafisa mwilaya. Nasha nafimbapo bwino-bwino na kabili. Nabutukila ku lukungu lwa ŋanda no kulya ulukonde bwangu-bwangu. Iyi nkonde yali iyalowesha ukucila pa nkonde shonse isho nalilepo.

english:
The following day, when grandma was in the garden picking vegetables, I sneaked in and peered at the bananas.

Nearly all were ripe. I couldn’t help taking a bunch of four.

As I tiptoed towards the door, I heard grandma coughing outside. I just managed to hide the bananas under my dress and walked past her.
translation: Ubushiku bwakonkelepo, ilyo bamaama baile mwibala mu kuswa umusaalu, naile lushenshe mu kumona pa nkonde. Ninshi shonse shili mukupya. Efyo nasendelemo shine. Cilya ndebendelela ku ciibi, naumfwa bamaama baleekoola panse. Efyo nafishile inkonde mwilaya no kuya pita epobaali.

english:
The following day was market day. Grandma woke up early. She always took ripe bananas and cassava to sell at the market.

I did not hurry to visit her that day. But I could not avoid her for long.
translation: Ubushiku bwakonkelepo, bwali buushiku bwakushitisha ku maliketi. Bamaama babukile lucelocelo. Baaletwala inkonde ishapya na tute lyonse mu kushitisha ku maliketi. Nshaceleele mu kubamona ubo bushiku, nomba nalibafulwike.

english:
Later that evening I was called by my mother and father, and Grandma. I knew why.

That night as I lay down to sleep, I knew I could never steal again, not from grandma, not from my parents, and certainly not from anyone else.
translation: Mu cungulo, bamaayo, bataata na bamaama balinjitile. Naishiba ne lyashi. Ubushiku bulya lintu naile mu kusendama, nasambilile ukuti nshakabwekeshepo ukwibila bamaama, abafyashi bandi nangu umuntu umbi na kabili.

english: Tom carries a tray of ripe bananas.
translation: Tom alasenda ulupe lwa nkonde ishapya.

english: Tom goes to the market to sell bananas.
translation: Tom alaya ku maliketi mu kushitisha inkonde.

english: People at the market are buying fruit.

But no one is buying

Tom’s bananas.

They prefer to buy fruit from women.
translation: Nomba tapali nangu umo uuleshita kuli Tomu.

english: “In our community, only women sell fruit,” people say. “What kind of a man is this?” people ask.
translation: “Mu mushi wesu, banamaayofye ebashitisha ifitwalo,” efilanda abantu. “Mwaume wa musango shani uyu?” efyo bepusha.

english:
But Tom does not give up.

He calls, “Buy my bananas!

Buy my sweet ripe bananas!”
translation: Nomba Tomu taleka. Aleeta abantu, “Shiteni inkonde shandi! Shiteni inkonde shandi ishapya kabili ishalowa!”

english:
One woman picks up a bunch of bananas from the tray.

She looks at the bananas carefully.
translation: Namaayo umo asendapo inkonde shimo pa lupe. Ashilolekesha bwino-bwino.

english:
More people come to the stall.

They buy Tom’s bananas and eat them.
translation: Abantu abengi baisa pali Tomu. Balashita inkonde shakwa Tomu no kushilya.

english:
Soon, the tray is empty.

Tom counts the money he earned.
translation: Ukwabula ukupoosa inshita, inkonde shapwa mu lupe. Tomu apenda indalama apanga.

english:
Then Tom buys soap, sugar, and bread.

He puts the things in his tray.
translation: Tomu ashitamo isopo, shuga no mukate. Afibiika mu lupe.

english: Tom balances the tray on his head and goes home.
translation: Tomu alaatengeseela ulupe lwakwe pa mutwe no kubwelela ku ŋanda.

english:
Sakima lived with his parents and his four year old sister.

They lived on a rich man’s land.

Their grass-thatched hut was at the end of a row of trees.
translation: Sakima aaleikala na bafyashi bakwe pamo na nkashi yakwe uwamyaka ine. Baleikala pancende ya mukankaala umo. Iŋanda yabo iyafyani yabeleele kumpela ya miti.

english:
When Sakima was three years old, he fell sick and lost his sight.

Sakima was a talented boy.
translation: Ilyo Sakima aali ne myaka itatu, alipofwile ku mulandu wa bulwele. Sakima aali mulumendo uwakwete icabupe.

english:
Sakima did many things that other six year old boys did not do.

For example, he could sit with older members of the village and discuss important matters.
translation: Sakima aaleecita ifintu ifingi efyo abalumendo bamyaka mutanda baaleefilwa. Ico mwingamwenako cimo cakuti, uyu Sakima aaleikala pa bakulu bamumushi no kulanshanya pa milandu iikankaala.

english:
The parents of Sakima worked at the rich man’s house.

They left home early in the morning and returned late in the evening.

Sakima was left with his little sister.
translation: Abafyashi bakwa Sakima baaleebomba pa ŋanda ya mukankaala. Baaleefuma pa ŋanda ku macaaca no kubwela inshita ya bushiku. Sakima aaleeshaala na nkashi yakwe.

english:
Sakima loved to sing songs.

One day his mother asked him, “Where do you learn these songs from, Sakima?”
translation: Sakima aalitemenwe ukwimba inyimbo. Ubushiku bumo banyina balimwipwishe abati, “Usambilila kwisa ishi nyimbo, Sakima?”

english: Sakima answered, “They just come, mother. I hear them in my head and then I sing.”
translation: Sakima ayaswike ati “Shiisafye, maayo, nshumfwa mu mutwe elyo nashimba.”

english:
Sakima liked to sing for his little sister, especially, if she felt hungry.

His sister would listen to him singing his favourite song.

She would sway to the soothing tune.
translation: Sakima alitemenwe ukwimbila nkashi yakwe, maka-maka nkashi yakwe nga aumfwa insala. Nkashi yakwe aaleekutika uko Sakima aleimba ulwimbo atemenwe saana, ninshi ayamba ukuisunsuntila ku ciunda ca lwimbo.

english:
“Can you sing it again and again, Sakima,” his sister would beg him.

Sakima would accept and sing it over and over again.
translation: Nkanshi yakwe aaleemulomba ati, “Njimbilako na kabili, Sakima.” Sakima aaleesumina no kubwekeshapo ukwimba ulwimbo imiku iingi.

english:
One evening when his parents returned home, they were very quiet.

Sakima knew that there was something wrong.
translation: Ubushiku bumo ilyo abafyashi bakwe baabwelele pa ŋanda, baalifye tondolo. Sakima aalishibe ukutiila pali ifyalubene.

english:
“What is wrong, mother, father?” Sakima asked.

Sakima learned that the rich man’s son was missing.

The man was very sad and lonely.
translation: “Finshi ifilubene, maayo, taata?” efyo aabepwishe. Sakima Baamwebele ukutiila umwana wa mukankaala aalilubile. Umukankaala aali no bulanda nganshi kabili aalifye eka bulanda-bulanda.

english:
“I can sing for him. He might be happy again,” Sakima told his parents.

But his parents dismissed him.

“He is very rich. You are only a blind boy. Do you think your song will help him?”
translation: “Kuti namwimbilako. Limbi kuti asansamuka na kabili,” efyo Sakima aebele abafyashi bakwe. Nomba abafyashi bakwe balikene. Abati, “Uyu muntu mukankaala saana. Iwe uli mwaice kabili taumona. Uleetontokanya ukutiila ulwimbo lobe kuti lwamwafwilisha?”

english:
However, Sakima did not give up.

His little sister supported him.

She said, “Sakima’s songs soothe me when I am hungry. They will soothe the rich man too.”
translation: Sakima taanenwiike. Nkashi yakwe aalimulandiileko. Aatiile, “Inyimbo shakwa Sakima shilantalalika nga ndi ne nsala. No mukankaala wine kuti shamutalalika. ”

english: The following day, Sakima asked his little sister to lead him to the rich man’s house.
translation: Ubushiku bwakonkelepo, Sakima aebele nkashi yakwe ukumutungulula ku ŋanda ya mukankaala.

english:
He stood below one big window and began to sing his favourite song.

Slowly, the head of the rich man began to show through the big window.
translation: Aiminine mwisamba lye windo ilikalamba no kwamba ukwimba ulwimbo aatemwishishe. Panoono-panoono, umutwe wa mukankaala wayambile ukumoneka pa windo.

english:
The workers stopped what they were doing. They listened to Sakima’s beautiful song.

But one man said, “Nobody has been able to console the boss. Does this blind boy think he will console him?”
translation: Ababomfi baaleekele imilimo yabo. Baaleekutika ku lwimbo lwakwa Sakima ulwawama nganshi. Nomba shitaata umo aatiile, “Tapaaba nangu umo uwakwanisha ukutalalika ba bwana. Bushe uyu mulumendo wapofula aleemona kwati kuti abatalalika?”

english:
Sakima finished singing his song and turned to leave.

But the rich man rushed out and said, “Please sing again.”
translation: Sakima alipwishishe ukwimba ulwimbo lwakwe kabili alimine ukuti aleeya ku mwabo. Nomba umukankaala alifumine panse no kutiila “Napaapaata, imba na kabili.”

english:
At that very moment, two men came carrying someone on a stretcher.

They had found the rich man’s son beaten up and left on the side of the road.
translation: Apopeene kwaishile abantu babili nabasenda umuntu pa macila. Baasangile umwana wa mukankaala nabamupuma ku fipondo kabili bamushiile mumbali ya musebo.

english:
The rich man was so happy to see his son again.

He rewarded Sakima for consoling him.

He took his son and Sakima to hospital so Sakima could regain his sight.
translation: Umukankaala aalisansamwike pa kumona umwana wakwe na kabili. Aalilambwile Sakima pa kumutalalika ku mutima. Aatwele umwana wakwe na Sakima ku cipataala mu kumona nga kuti Sakima atampa ukumona na kabili.

english: The small bus stop in my village was busy with people and overloaded buses. On the ground were even more things to load. Touts were shouting the names where their buses were going.
translation: Pa citesheni ca saaca mu mushi wandi pali abantu abengi na basaaca abaiswilemo abantu. Panshi napo ninshi pali ifipe na fimbi ifyakulonga. Abalumendo ninshi baleependilila ukuleya basaaca.

english: “City! City! Going west!” I heard a tout shouting. That was the bus I needed to catch.
translation: “Ku kalale! Ku kalale! Abaleya ku masamba!” Naumfwile baleepunda. Eesaaca nalingile ukuniina.

english: The city bus was almost full, but more people were still pushing to get on. Some packed their luggage under the bus. Others put theirs on the racks inside.
translation: Saaca yaaleeya ku kalaale ninshi ili mukwisula, nomba abantu beena ninshi bacili balelwisha ukuniina. Bambi baalongele ifipe munshi ya saaca. Bambi baalongele pa tushimbi twa mukati ka saaca.

english: New passengers clutched their tickets as they looked for somewhere to sit in the crowded bus. Women with young children made them comfortable for the long journey.
translation: Abaaleniina baikatiliile utumatikiti lintu baalefwaya apakwikala muli saaca iyaiswile abantu. Banamaayo abaali na baana baafwaile abaana babo apakwikala bwino pa bulendo ubutali.

english: I squeezed in next to a window. The person sitting next to me was holding tightly to a green plastic bag. He wore old sandals, a worn out coat, and he looked nervous.
translation: Naifyantike mupeepi ne windo. Abo naikeele nabo mupeepi baikete akacola ka pulashitiki akakatapakatapa. Baafwele indyato ishakale ne jaketi ilyapwa kabili baaleemoneka mwenso-mwenso.

english: I looked outside the bus and realised that I was leaving my village, the place where I had grown up. I was going to the big city.
translation: Naloleshe panse ya saaca elyo caisa mu maano ukuti ciine-ciine naaleefuma mu mushi wandi, incende nakuliilemo. Naleeya ku musumba ukulu.

english: The loading was completed and all passengers were seated. Hawkers still pushed their way into the bus to sell their goods to the passengers. Everyone was shouting the names of what was available for sale. The words sounded funny to me.
translation: Bapwisha ukulonga na bantu bonse baikala. Abakushitisha ninshi bacili balepitana muli saaca mu kushitisha utwamakwebo yabo ku bantu. Cila muntu alepunda amashina yafyo aaleeshitisha. Aya mashiwi baaleelanda yaaleesekesha.

english: A few passengers bought drinks, others bought small snacks and began to chew. Those who did not have any money, like me, just watched.
translation: Abalendo abanoono baashitile ifyakunwa, bambi bashita utwakulya batampa no kulya. Abashakwete indalama nga ine baletambakofye.

english: These activities were interrupted by the hooting of the bus, a sign that we were ready to leave. The tout yelled at the hawkers to get out.
translation: Ukushitisha no kushita kwapumfyanishiwe lintu uuta ya saacai yalilile, ukulangisha ukuti yaali mukwima. Kondakita epakupundilila bakashitisha bonse ukuti bekile muli saaca.

english: Hawkers pushed each other to make their way out of the bus. Some gave back change to the travellers. Others made last minute attempts to sell more items.
translation: Bakashitisha balasunkana pa kufuma muli bashi. Bambi baleebwesesha cenji ku baali pa bulendo. Bambi nabo balelwisha ukushitishako ifyakulekelesha.

english: As the bus left the bus stop, I stared out of the window. I wondered if I would ever go back to my village again.
translation: Cilya saaca yafuma mu citesheni, nalaalolesha pa windo. Nalaatontokanya nga cakuti nkatala nkabwelelemo ku mushi na kabili.

english: As the journey progressed, the inside of the bus got very hot. I closed my eyes hoping to sleep.
translation: Cilya tuleya, muli saaca mwakaba. Naisala amenso ukuti ningashipulako.

english: But my mind drifted back home. Will my mother be safe? Will my rabbits fetch any money? Will my brother remember to water my tree seedlings?
translation: Nomba amaano yandi yabwelela ku ŋanda. Bushe bamaayo bakekala umutende? Bushe bakalulu bandi bakashitishiwa? Bushe ndume yandi akulaibukisha ukutapilila utumuti twandi?

english: On the way, I memorised the name of the place where my uncle lived in the big city. I was still mumbling it when I fell asleep.
translation: Mu nshila naya ndesungila ishina lya ncende ukwaleikala bayaama mu kalaale. Ncili ndeilumbula mu kapoopo naponena mutulo.

english: Nine hours later, I woke up with loud banging and calling for passengers going back to my village. I grabbed my small bag and jumped out of the bus.
translation: Panuma yansa pabula, nabukila mu congo cabalepunda no kupumpusha ukwita abaleebwekelamo ku mushi wesu. Nasompola akacoola no kufuma muli saaca.

english: The return bus was filling up quickly. Soon it would make its way back east. The most important thing for me now, was to start looking for my uncle’s house.
translation: Bwangu-bwangu saaca yakubwelelamo yayaileisula. Nombalinefye yalaima ukubwekelamo kukabanga. Icaali icikalamba kuli ine pali ii nshita kwamba ukufwaya iŋanda ya bayaama.

english: One elephant is going to drink water.
translation: Insofu imo ileeya mu kunwa ameenshi.

english: Two giraffes are going to drink water.
translation: Indyabuluba shibili shileeya mu kunwa ameenshi.

english: Three buffaloes and four birds are also going to drink water.
translation: Imboo shitatu ne fyuni fine nafyo fileeya mu kunwa ameenshi.

english: Five impalas and six warthogs are walking to the water.
translation: Impombo shisaano na bamunjili mutanda baleeya ku meenshi.

english: Seven zebras are running to the water.
Eight frogs and nine fish are swimming in the water.
translation: Baacuula cine-konse-konse ne sabi pabula fileesamba mu menshi.

english: One lion roars. He also wants to drink. Who is afraid of the lion?
translation: Inkalamo imo yabuluma. Nayo ileefwaya ukunwa ameenshi. Naani aletiina inkalamo?

english: One elephant is drinking water with the lion.
translation: Insofu imo ilenwa ameenshi ne nkalamo.

english:
Once upon a time,
there lived a happy
family.
translation: Patiile akantu, kwali ulupwa ulwaikeele mu mutende ne nsansa.

english:
They never fought with
each other. They helped
their parents at home
and in the fields.
translation: Tabatalile abalwa beka-beka. Baaleeyafwa abafyashi baabo pa ŋanda na mwibala.

english:
But they were not
allowed to go near a
fire.

They had to do all their
work during the night.

Because they were made of wax!
translation: Baaleebomba imilimo yabo yonse ubushiku. Pantu bapangilwe ne pula.

english:
But one of the boys
longed to go out in the
sunlight.
translation: Nomba umo pa balumendo aaleefwaisha ukuya panse mu kasuba.

english:
One day the longing
was too strong. His
brothers warned him…
translation: Ubushiku bumo icakufwaya ukuya pa kusuba cacilamo. Bandume yakwe baalimusokele…

english:
But it was too late!
He melted in the hot
sun.
translation: Nomba balicelelwe. Asunguluka mu kasuba kaakaba.

english:
The wax children were
so sad to see their
brother melting away.
translation: Abaana bepula baali no bulanda pa kumona uko ndume nabo aleesunguluka.

english:
But they made a plan.
They shaped the lump
of melted wax into a
bird.
translation: Nomba baalyumfwene. Baapangile icuuni ukufuma kwipula ilyasungulwike.

english:
They took their bird
brother up to a high
mountain.
translation: Baasendele ndume nabo bapangile mu cuuni pa muulu wa lupili ulutali.

english:
And as the sun rose, he
flew away singing into
the morning light.
translation: Lilya akasuba katula, aalipupwike aya aleimba mu cengelo ca lucelo.

english: One day, mama got a lot of fruit.
translation: Ubushiku bumo bamaayo balikwete ifisabo ifingi.

english:
“When can we have some fruit?” we ask.

“We will have the fruit tonight,” says mama.
translation: Twaipusha ati, “Ni nshitanshi twalalyapo ifitwalo?” Bamaayo abati, “Tuleelya ifitwalo ubushiku.”

english: My brother Rahim is greedy. He tastes all the fruit. He eats a lot of it.
translation: Ndume yandi Rahim alifunuka. Alyako ku fitwalo fyonse. Aalya ifingi.

english:
“Look at what Rahim did!” shouts my little brother.

“Rahim is naughty and selfish,” I say.
translation: “Moneni ifyo Rahim acitile,” efyapundile kandume yandi. Nayasuka nati, “Rahim toomfwa kabili aliitemwa.”

english: We are also angry with Rahim. But Rahim is not sorry.
translation: Na ifwe bonse naatumufulilwa Rahim. Nomba Rahim tasakamene.

english: “Aren’t you going to punish Rahim?” asks little brother.
translation: Akaice kandi kaipusha akati, “Bushe tamwamukande Rahim?”

english: “Rahim, soon you will be sorry,” warns mama.
“My tummy is so sore,” whispers Rahim.
Mama knew this would happen. The fruit is punishing Rahim!
translation: Bamaayo baalishibe ukuti ifi efyali no kucitika. Ifitwalo filekanda Rahim.

english:
Later, Rahim says sorry to us. “I will never be so greedy again,” he promises.

And we all believe him.
translation: Panuma, Rahim alomba ubwelelo kuli ifwe. Alaya ati, “Nshakafunuke na kabili.” Bonse twamusuminisha. Takabwekeshepo icimusango cakuitemwa.
